question: What penalty does a driver get for entering the pit lane during the race while it is closed, without needing essential repairs?
expected_answer: A Stop-and-Go Penalty (during a TTCS, i.e. Sprint or Race).

question: How is a 5-second time penalty served during a race?
expected_answer: The driver must enter the pit lane at their next pit entry, stop in their designated pit stop position for at least five seconds, and then rejoin; the car may not be worked on (touching car or driver counts) until it has been stationary for the full penalty. If the driver makes no further pit stop, 5 seconds are added to their elapsed time instead.
correction: [Gold review] Added B1.9.6 (procedure for serving penalties) as alternative. Suggest verifier also adds to the answer: may elect not to serve if no further pit stop, then 5 s added. question: What happens if a drive-through penalty is imposed during the last three laps of a race?
expected_answer: 20 seconds are added to the driver's elapsed time (30 seconds for a Stop-and-Go Penalty).

question: What penalties can the stewards give for an incident during qualifying?
expected_answer: They may delete the driver's lap time(s) or drop the driver a number of grid positions; grid penalties are served in the Race (or the Sprint if the infringement was in Sprint Qualifying).

question: How long is SQ1 in Sprint Qualifying and how many cars are eliminated at the end of it?
expected_answer: 12 minutes; the slowest six cars are eliminated.

question: How long are Q1, Q2 and Q3 in 2026 qualifying?
expected_answer: Q1 18 minutes, Q2 15 minutes, Q3 13 minutes, with seven-minute breaks between them.

question: What is the distance of a sprint?
expected_answer: The least number of complete laps that exceed 100 km.

question: What is the maximum time a sprint can run, including if it is suspended?
expected_answer: One hour from the start signal; if suspended, the suspension time is added up to a maximum total of 1.5 hours.

question: What is the scheduled race distance in 2026, and is Monaco different?
expected_answer: The least number of complete laps exceeding 305 km; in Monaco it is the least number exceeding 260 km.

question: From how long before FP1 are screens or covers that hide the cars banned?
expected_answer: From 29 hours before the scheduled start of FP1 (unless needed solely for mechanical reasons, e.g. fire protection).

question: How many times per championship can a team request to replace front wing, rear wing, rear bodywork or floor bodywork with parts of a different design under parc fermé?
expected_answer: Six (6) times, provided the replacement is a specification previously used in pre-season testing, a qualifying session or a race/sprint.

question: By how much is a race shortened after an aborted start procedure?
expected_answer: By one lap for each Aborted Start procedure.

question: What happens if the Safety Car is still deployed at the start of the last lap?
expected_answer: It enters the pit lane at the end of the lap (unless the Race Director decides otherwise) and cars take the chequered flag without overtaking; the Safety Car's orange lights are switched off as the signal.

question: How many sets of dry, intermediate and wet tyres may each driver use at a standard format competition without ICTT?
expected_answer: 13 dry-weather sets, 5 intermediate sets and 2 wet-weather sets (12 dry sets at sprint or ICTT weekends).
correction: [Gold review] Added B6.2.4 (tyre allocation table: 2+3+8 = 13 dry, 5 inter, 2 wet) as alternative.

question: How many engines (ICE), turbochargers and exhaust sets can each driver use in the 2026 championship?
expected_answer: 3 ICE, 3 turbochargers and 3 exhaust sets (with an additional unit allowed under B8.2.3 conditions).

question: What grid penalty applies when a driver uses more power unit elements than allowed?
expected_answer: 10 grid places the first time an additional element of each type is used, then 5 grid places each subsequent time; penalties are cumulative.

question: What happens when a race is suspended with a red flag?
expected_answer: Overtaking is forbidden, the pit lane exit is closed and all cars must proceed slowly into the pit lane, lining up in the fast lane behind the first car.

question: What is the minimum mass of a 2026 Formula 1 car?
expected_answer: 724 kg plus the Nominal Tyre Mass; 726 kg plus Nominal Tyre Mass during Sprint Qualifying and Qualifying (increased further under a Heat Hazard).

question: What is the maximum electrical power of the ERS-K in 2026?
expected_answer: 350 kW (absolute DC power).

question: What is the fuel energy flow limit for the 2026 power unit?
expected_answer: 3000 MJ/h, with no cylinder exceeding 550 MJ/h under normal operating conditions.

question: What engine capacity is required in 2026?
How many forward gears must a 2026 car have?
expected_answer: Eight forward gear ratios; continuously variable transmissions are not permitted.

expected_answer: 3400 mm (at Legality Setup).

question: What kind of fuel must be used under the 2026 technical regulations?
expected_answer: Advanced Sustainable (AS) fuels made solely of AS components; co-processing is not permitted.

question: How far may the front wing flaps move when the front wing adjuster is used?
expected_answer: Maximum deviation of 30 mm for the FW Primary Flap and 60 mm for the FW Secondary Flap.

question: What is the maximum and minimum number of competitions in the championship?
expected_answer: Maximum 24, minimum 8.

question: How many cars can take part in the championship?
expected_answer: No more than 24 cars, with two cars entered by each team.

question: Which competition numbers can drivers use?
expected_answer: 1 to 99 inclusive, except 17.

question: Who may use car number 1?
expected_answer: The reigning World Champion Driver; their previous number is reserved for them if they lose the title.

question: How many points does the winner get if the leader completed at least two laps but less than 25% of the race distance?
expected_answer: 6 points (column 1 scale: 6, 4, 3, 2, 1 for the top five).

question: What is the fine if the top three drivers don't attend the FIA Prize Giving Ceremony?
expected_answer: Up to €250,000 for each failure to comply (except in case of Force Majeure), payable by the team.

question: Can teams change their car setup after qualifying?
expected_answer: No. Cars are in parc fermé; only the permitted work is allowed. Breaching parc fermé means starting from the pit lane.

question: If it's pouring rain at the start, what happens?
expected_answer: The formation lap(s) may be started behind the Safety Car (signalled at the 10-minute signal), and wet-weather tyres become compulsory.
correction: [Gold review] Added B5.10.1, the dedicated clause for starting behind the Safety Car when track conditions are unsuitable.

question: Do laps behind the safety car count toward the race distance?
expected_answer: Yes, each lap completed behind the Safety Car counts as a race lap (VSC laps also count).

question: What's the longest a Grand Prix can go on for?
expected_answer: Two hours from the start signal; with a red-flag suspension the total can reach a maximum of three hours.

question: What happens if a driver lines up badly in their grid box at the start?
expected_answer: Cars must be stationary and positioned so no part of the front tyre contact patch is outside the box lines; the stewards can give a 5-second, 10-second, drive-through or stop-and-go penalty.
correction: [Gold Review] Stewards can also give a Stop-and-Go Penalty in such a case. | [Moved into answer] Verifier addition moved into expected_answer: Stop-and-Go Penalty is also possible (B5.11.1).

question: If someone stalls on the formation lap, can the cars behind overtake them?
expected_answer: Only to avoid unduly delaying the field and only to re-establish the original order; a delayed driver who can't regain position before the first safety car line must start from the pit lane, or get a Stop-and-Go Penalty.

question: Can a car reverse in the pit lane?
expected_answer: No, at no time may a car be reversed in the pit lane under its own power.

expected_answer: Driver Adjustable Bodywork adjusts both the front wing profiles and rear wing flap via the FIA Standard ECU; Corner Mode = deactivated; the driver may only activate it when notified that it is enabled (partial activation only in low-grip conditions).
